Six days ago, Apple released the first developer beta of iOS 27.2, skipping iOS 27.1 beta. Following yesterday's release of developer beta 2, Apple has now rolled out the first public beta of iOS 27.2, which includes an all-new iPhone Health app. Apple has also opened up the ability to book and purchase lab services through Quest Diagnostics via the new Health app.

iOS 27.2 beta brings a redesigned Health app and more

iOS 27.2 is the version following iOS 27, which launched on September 14. iOS 27.1 is only available for iPhone Duo.

Apple has previously detailed how the iOS 27.1 SDK lets developers take full advantage of iPhone Duo's display. You can see here how apps display on iPhone Duo depending on the iOS version they target.

On Friday, Apple released Xcode 27.1 beta, adding an iPhone Duo simulator and app development support for the new foldable iPhone.

The first iOS 27.2 developer beta includes the following updates:

  • The redesigned Health app, first unveiled by Apple at the iPhone 18 Pro event, is now live in this beta.
  • Group FaceTime gains dual-camera simultaneous capture.
  • Siri AI language support adds French, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese, and Spanish.
  • Apple TV app profiles arrive on iPhone.
  • In Apple Podcasts, "Up Next" has been renamed to "New Episodes," with "Continue Playing" moved directly below "New Episodes." Podcast episode lists now match their show's accent color.
  • Apple Music now uses fewer icon colors as label accents within the app.

iOS 27.2 is expected to launch officially in October. For now, both iPhone developers and public beta users can get an early look at the new Apple Health app.
